chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Husayn Bin Usman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, maintaining kinship purifies the deeds, increases the wealth, eases the Reckoning, repels the afflictions, and increases the sustenance.

key_terms.صِلَةَ الرَّحِمِ: Maintaining kinship ties / Goodly relationship with relatives

ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of maintaining kinship ties in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores silat al-rahim as a comprehensive mechanism for both spiritual purification and material prosperity, linking familial duty directly to divine ease in the afterlife. Scholars often interpret the 'purification of deeds' as removing minor sins through the act of kindness, while 'facilitating the accounting' reflects the belief that strong family ties serve as a shield against divine reckoning. This dual benefit highlights the Islamic view that social cohesion is integral to individual spiritual and economic well-being.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Husayn Bin Usman, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The goodly relationships purify the deeds, and develops the wealth, and eases the Reckoning, and repels the afflictions, and increases in the sustenance’.
en.sarwar: 33. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Husayn ibn ‘Uthman from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Maintaining good relations with relatives cleanses the deeds, increases wealth, eases off the giving of accounts on the Day of Judgment, repels misfortunes and increases one’s means of sustenance.”
